title: Cantar de mio Cid
titleEn: The Song of the Cid — The king proposes the marriages and a meeting with the Cid (tirada 102, lines 1885–1958)
part: Tirada 102 · The king proposes the marriages and a meeting with the Cid (lines 1885–1958)
source: Ramón Menéndez Pidal (ed.), Poema de mio Cid, 2.ª edición corregida (Clásicos Castellanos 24; Madrid: Ediciones de “La Lectura”, 1923), pp. 248–252, lines 1885–1958 (tiradas 102–102). Text follows Pidal's critical text exactly, including its old accentuation and mixed spellings; Pidal's italics (his editorial restorations) are shown in [brackets], and a line he restores whole is flagged in its note. Line numbers are Pidal's. Pronunciation convention: reconstructed twelfth-century Castilian. Translations made fresh from the Old Spanish; Pidal's notes and vocabulary (1908–11) the lexical aids.

sentences.i: “We ask a grace of you, as of our king and lord: with your counsel we wish to do this — that you ask the Campeador for his daughters on our behalf; we wish to marry them, to his honour and to our own profit.”
sentences.n: Tirada 102 (assonance ó) — The Infantes get the king to negotiate the marriage for them; the king asks for a meeting with the Çid; Minaya returns to Valencia and tells the Çid everything; the Çid fixes the place of the meeting (Pidal: Los infantes logran que el rey les trate el casamiento. El rey pide vistas con el Cid.—Minaya vuelve a Valencia, y entera al Cid de todo.—El Cid fija el lugar de las vistas). The line-ends señor, nos, Campeador, pro carry a stressed ó, held through all the tirada's verses. The speakers are the Infantes of Carrión, whose coming to the king closed the previous part (v. 1884). Merced vos pidimos, 'we ask you a grace'; commo a rey e a señor, 'as (one asks) of king and lord'. fer = fazer, 'to do' (f- for h-, modern hacer); nos, 'we', the subject pronoun set last for weight. demandedes, present subjunctive (= demandéis), 'that you ask for (them) for us'. y, here 'and'. a su ondra y a nuestra pro, 'to his honour and to our profit': pro, 'profit, advantage', feminine. For the pride of the Carrión family Pidal refers to his introduction (p. 91).

sentences.t: Una grant ora, el rey penssó e comidió:
sentences.l: One great hour, the king thought and pondered:
sentences.i: For a long while the king thought and pondered:
sentences.n: Pidal's note: 'el rey pensó y meditó un gran rato', 'the king thought and meditated a long while': una grant ora is 'a long while', not a clock hour. comidió, preterite of comedir, 'to ponder, weigh'. The same verse comes back for the Çid at v. 1932, when the same proposal reaches him.

sentences.t:
“Yo eché de tierra al buen Campeador,
e faziendo yo a él mal, e él a mí grand pro,
del casamiento non sé sis abrá sabor;
mas pues bos lo queredes, entremos en la razón.”
sentences.l:
“I cast out of land to-the good Campeador,
and doing I to him harm, and he to me great profit,
of-the marriage not I-know if-himself he-will-have liking;
but since you it want, let-us-enter into the matter.”
sentences.i: “I drove the good Campeador out of the land, and while I was doing him harm he was doing me great good; I do not know whether this marriage will be to his liking. But since you wish it, let us take the matter up.”
sentences.n: echar de tierra, 'to cast out of the land', the poem's word for the exile; al buen Campeador, the personal object marked with a. faziendo yo a él mal, e él a mí grand pro, a gerund clause with its subject spoken (yo), the second half borrowing the same verb: the king owns his wrong plainly. Pidal's note: 'no sé si gustará del casamiento', 'I do not know if he will like the marriage'. sis = si se, the se adding nothing in English; aver sabor de, 'to have a liking for, to wish', abrá its future. bos = vos, so spelled here. Pidal's note: entremos en la razón, 'comencemos la plática', 'let us begin the talk' (compare v. 1926); razón, 'speech, matter'.

sentences.t:
A Minaya Álbar Fáñez e a Per Vermu[doz]
el rey don Alfonsso essora los llamó,
a una quadra elle los apartó:
sentences.l:
To Minaya Álbar Fáñez and to Per Vermu[doz]
the king don Alfonsso then them called,
to a chamber he them took-aside:
sentences.i: Then King Alfonso called Minaya Álvar Fáñez and Per Vermudoz to him, and drew them aside into a chamber:
sentences.n: A Minaya … e a Per Vermu[doz] … los llamó, the two men named first with a and taken up again by los. Per Vermu[doz], the doz Pidal's (in italics), as at vv. 1897, 1907 and 1919. essora, 'then, at that hour' (esa hora). quadra, 'a room, chamber'. elle = él, the fuller form of the pronoun. apartó, 'took aside': what the king says next is for their ears alone.

sentences.t:
“Oídme Minaya e vos, Per Vermu[doz]:
sírvem mio Çid [Roi Díaz] Campeador,
el[le] lo mereçe e de mí abrá perdón;
viniéssem a vistas si oviesse dent sabor.
sentences.l:
“Hear-me Minaya and you, Per Vermu[doz]:
serves-me my Çid [Roi Díaz] Campeador,
h[e] it deserves and from me he-will-have pardon;
let-him-come-to-me to meeting if he-had of-it liking.
sentences.i: “Hear me, Minaya, and you, Per Vermudoz: my Çid Ruy Díaz the Campeador serves me; he has earned it, and he shall have my pardon. Let him come to meet me, if he has a mind to.
sentences.n: Oídme, imperative + me. sírvem = sírveme, 'he serves me', the e of me squeezed out. [Roi Díaz], both words Pidal's (in italics): Roi, another spelling of Roy, 'Ruy'. el[le], the le Pidal's (in italics). de mí abrá perdón, 'from me he will have pardon': the king's word for the end of the exile. 1899b is Pidal's own number. Pidal's note: 'venga a vistas conmigo, si gusta', 'let him come to a meeting with me, if he likes'. viniéssem = viniesse me, imperfect subjunctive with me, a wish; vistas, 'a meeting, an interview' between lords (literally 'sights'). dent, 'of it' (= de ello), with aver sabor: 'if he had the wish for it'.

sentences.t:
Otros mandados ha en esta mi cort:
Di[da]go e Ferrando, los iffantes de Carrión,
sabor han de casar con sus fijas amas a dos.
sentences.l:
Other messages there-is in this my court:
Di[da]go and Ferrando, the infantes of Carrión,
liking they-have to marry with his daughters both two.
sentences.i: There is other business at this court of mine: Diego and Fernando, the Infantes of Carrión, wish to marry his two daughters.
sentences.n: mandados, 'messages, business to be carried'. ha, 'there is' (aver of existence, modern hay). esta mi cort, demonstrative + possessive together, like article + possessive. Di[da]go, the da Pidal's (in italics): Diego; Ferrando = Fernando. Pidal's note to v. 1938 adds that the historical Diego and Fernán González appear in royal charters of 1090 and 1105. sabor han de casar, 'they have a wish to marry' (aver sabor again). amas a dos, 'both the two' (amas = ambas).

sentences.t:
Se[e]d buenos mensageros, e ruégovoslo yo
que gelo digades al buen Campeador:
abrá y ondra e creçrá en onor,
por conssagrar con iffantes de Carrión.”
sentences.l:
Be good messengers, and I-beg-you-it I
that to-him-it you-say to-the good Campeador:
he-will-have there honour and will-grow in estate,
for to-become-kin with infantes of Carrión.”
sentences.i: Be good messengers, and I beg you to tell this to the good Campeador: there will be honour in it for him, and he will grow in lands and lordship by becoming kin to the Infantes of Carrión.”
sentences.n: Se[e]d, imperative of seer (= sed, 'be'), the second e Pidal's (in italics). ruégovoslo = ruego + vos + lo, 'I beg it of you'. gelo = ge + lo, 'it to him' (modern se lo), the him then named: al buen Campeador. y, 'there, in it'. ondra, 'honour, standing'; onor, 'estate, lordship held', the lands that go with rank. creçrá, future of creçer with the vowel dropped (= crecerá). Pidal's note: conssagrar, for consagrar, 'emparentar con relación de suegro a yerno' o 'de yerno a suegro', 'to become kin as father-in-law to son-in-law', or the reverse (compare v. 3356); por + infinitive, 'through, by'.

sentences.i: Minaya spoke, and Per Vermudoz agreed: “We will put to him what you say; afterwards let the Çid do as he pleases.”
sentences.n: plogo a Per Vermu[doz], 'it pleased Per Vermudoz' (plogo, preterite of plazer): Minaya speaks for both, his companion assents. Rogar gelo emos, the split future, rogaremos with gelo lodged between infinitive and ending (emos = hemos): 'we will ask it of him'. faga = haga, subjunctive of command, 'let him do'. oviere, future subjunctive of aver: lo que oviere sabor, 'whatever he may wish'.

sentences.t:
—“Dezid a R[o]y Díaz, el que en buen ora [naçió],
quel iré a vistas do aguisado f[o]re;
do el[le] dixiere, y sea el mojón.
Andar le quiero a mio Çid en toda pro.”
sentences.l:
—“Say to R[o]y Díaz, he who in good hour [was-born],
that-to-him I-will-go to meeting where fitting it-may-be;
where h[e] may-say, there let-be the boundary-stone.
To-go for-him I-want to my Çid in all profit.”
sentences.i: “Tell Ruy Díaz, he who was born in a good hour, that I will come to meet him wherever it is fitting; wherever he says, there let the boundary-stone be set. I mean to stand by my Çid in all that is to his good.”
sentences.n: The king speaks again (Pidal's dash marks the change of speaker). R[o]y, the o Pidal's (in italics). el que en buen ora [naçió], 'he who was born in a good hour', the formula, its last word Pidal's restoration: the whole word is in italics on the scan (italic n and single-storey a, against the roman ora beside it). quel = que le. aguisado, 'fitting, arranged'; f[o]re = fuere, future subjunctive of ser, the o Pidal's (in italics). el[le], the le Pidal's. mojón, 'boundary-stone': the meeting-place, marked out like a frontier. Pidal's note: the Çid is to fix the place of the meeting and the king its date (vv. 1962, 1951). Andar le quiero … en toda pro, Pidal's note: 'quiero ayudar al Cid en cuanto pueda', 'I want to help the Çid in all I can' (compare v. 1388); le … a mio Çid, the pronoun and then the person.

sentences.t:
Espidiensse al rey, con esto tornados son,
van pora Valençia ellos e todos los sos.
sentences.l:
They-were-taking-leave of-the king, with this turned are,
they-go toward Valençia they and all the theirs.
sentences.i: They took their leave of the king and, with this, turned homeward; they make for Valencia, they and all their men.
sentences.n: Espidiensse = espidien se, 'they took their leave' (espedirse = despedirse), the imperfect in -ie as in vinien (v. 1884), with se. tornados son, 'they have turned back', ser + participle with a verb of motion. pora = para. los sos, 'their people', the possessive standing alone (sos = sus). Imperfect, perfect and present in one breath: the epic tense-mixing.

sentences.i: When the good Campeador learned of it, he mounted in haste and rode out to meet them; my Çid smiled and embraced them warmly:
sentences.n: sopo, preterite of saber, 'he came to know'. apriessa = aprisa, 'in haste'. cavalga (present) beside salió (preterite): tense-mixing again. sonrrisós = sonrrisó se, 'he smiled', the se cut to -s after the stressed vowel. abraçó = abrazó.

sentences.t:
“¿Venides, Minaya, e vos, Per Vermu[doz]!
En pocas tierras a tales dos varones.
¿Commo son las saludes de Alfons mio señor?
¿si es pagado o reçibió el don?”
sentences.l:
“Do-you-come, Minaya, and you, Per Vermu[doz]!
In few lands there-are such two men.
How are the greetings of Alfons my lord?
if he-is pleased or received the gift?”
sentences.i: “So you are come, Minaya, and you, Per Vermudoz! There are few lands that hold two such men. What news do you bring of Alfonso, my lord? Is he pleased? Did he receive the gift?”
sentences.n: ¿Venides …!, 'do you come?': a question that is a welcome, hence Pidal's opening ¿ and closing ! (his note compares v. 204 for the greeting put as a question). a = ha, 'there are' (aver of existence). varones, 'men of worth'; its ó, with an unstressed e after it, counts in the assonance. Pidal's note: '¿Qué noticias traes de Alfonso?', 'what news do you bring of Alfonso?' (compare v. 928): saludes are news of someone absent. Pidal's note to 1922: the conjunction si heads a direct question as if it were an indirect one ('tell me if he is pleased'; compare v. 3216). pagado, 'satisfied'. el don, the two hundred horses Minaya took to the king in the previous part.

sentences.t:
Dixo Minaya: “d' alma e de coraçón
es pagado, e davos su amor.”
Dixo mio Çid: “grado al Criador!”
sentences.l:
Said Minaya: “from soul and from heart
he-is pleased, and he-gives-you his love.”
Said my Çid: “thanks to-the Creator!”
sentences.i: Minaya said: “He is pleased with all his heart and soul, and he gives you his favour.” My Çid said: “Thanks be to the Creator!”
sentences.n: d' alma e de coraçón, 'with soul and heart', wholeheartedly. davos = da vos, 'he gives you'. amor, 'love', here the lord's grace toward a vassal. grado, 'thanks'.

sentences.t:
Esto diziendo, conpieçan la razón,
lo quel rogava Alfons el de León
de dar su[e]s fijas a ifantes de Carrión,
quel connosçie i ondra e creç[r]ié en onor,
que gelo conssejava d' alma e de coraçón.
sentences.l:
This saying, they-begin the speech,
that which-him was-asking Alfons he of León
of to-give hi[s] daughters to infantes of Carrión,
that-for-him he-recognized there honour and he-would-gro[w] in estate,
that to-him-it he-was-counselling from soul and from heart.
sentences.i: With this said, they begin the business: what Alfonso of León asked of him — that he give his daughters to the Infantes of Carrión; that the king saw honour in it for him, and that he would grow in lands and lordship; that he urged it on him with all his heart and soul.
sentences.n: Pidal's note to v. 1893 sends here: conpieçan la razón, 'they begin the talk' (conpieçan = comienzan). lo quel rogava, 'what he asked of him', quel = que le. Alfons el de León, 'Alfonso, he of León'. su[e]s, the e Pidal's (in italics): sues, an old form of sus. a ifantes, without the article. quel connosçie i ondra, 'that he saw honour for him in it': connosçie, imperfect of conosçer in -ie (= conocía), i, 'there, in it'; the clause gives back the king's words of v. 1905 in reported form, and taking the king as its subject is our reading. creç[r]ié, conditional of creçer (= crecería), the r Pidal's (in italics). gelo conssejava, 'he advised it to him'. The five verses hang loosely on conpieçan: the messengers' report, told rather than spoken.

sentences.t:
Quando lo oyó mio Çid el buen Campeador,
una grand ora penssó e comidió:
“Esto gradesco a Cristus el mio señor.
sentences.l:
When it heard my Çid the good Campeador,
one great hour he-thought and pondered:
“This I-thank to Cristus the my lord.
sentences.i: When my Çid the good Campeador heard it, for a long while he thought and pondered: “For this I give thanks to Christ my Lord.
sentences.n: una grand ora penssó e comidió, the king's own verse of v. 1889 ('thought and meditated a long while', Pidal). gradesco = agradezco, 'I give thanks for'. Cristus, the Latin form of the name. el mio señor, article + possessive.

sentences.t:
Echado fu de tierra, [h]e tollida la onor,
con grand afán gané lo que he yo;
a Dios lo gradesco que del rey he su [amor],
e pidenme mis fijas pora ifantes de Carrión.
sentences.l:
Cast-out I-was from land, I-[h]ave taken-away the estate,
with great toil I-won what have I;
to God it I-thank that from-the king I-have his [love],
and they-ask-me my daughters for infantes of Carrión.
sentences.i: I was driven out of the land and stripped of my lands and lordship; with great toil I won all I have. I thank God that I have the king's favour again, and now they ask me for my daughters for the Infantes of Carrión.
sentences.n: fu = fui, 'I was' (preterite of ser). [h]e, the h Pidal's (in italics): he, 'I have', with tollida, 'taken away', agreeing with la onor, 'I have (had) my estate taken'; without the h the word would be e, 'and'. onor, 'estate, lordship', as at v. 1905. afán, 'toil'. he, 'I have' (aver as full verb). del rey he su [amor], 'from the king I have his favour', the last word Pidal's (in italics). pidenme, 'they ask me for'. The speech runs on into the four restored verses that follow.

sentences.t:
¿Dezid, Minaya e vos Per Vermudoz,
d' aqueste casamiento que semeja a vos?”
—“Lo que a vos ploguiere esso dezimos nos.”
sentences.l:
Say, Minaya and you Per Vermudoz,
of this marriage what it-seems to you?”
—“That which to you may-please that we-say we.”
sentences.i: Tell me, Minaya, and you, Per Vermudoz, what do you think of this marriage?” “Whatever pleases you, that is what we say.”
sentences.n: These three verses and the next (1937e) are printed wholly in italics: they are Pidal's restoration, not the manuscript's. His footnote calls the first 1937b; the letters c–e are ours. The footnote does not say where the wording comes from; it speaks to the sense: the Çid consults his nephews (Pidal's word) about his daughters' marriage, but not Jimena, whom he tells only at v. 2188 that it is settled, although the power to marry the daughters lay with father and mother (Hinojosa); at v. 2606 Jimena shows her share in it, and the Primera Crónica General has the Çid consult his wife at this point. Dezid, imperative. aqueste = este. semeja, 'it seems'. ploguiere, future subjunctive of plazer. esso dezimos nos, 'that we say', the subject pronoun last.

sentences.i: The Çid said: “The Infantes of Carrión are of high birth; they are very proud, and they have a place at court. This marriage would not be to my liking;
sentences.n: 1937e is wholly Pidal's (in italics), the last of his four restored verses. natura, 'birth, lineage'. urgullosos = orgullosos, 'proud'. Pidal's note: an part en la cort does not mean they had seats in the Cortes (as Corominas read it, 1900) but that they regularly followed the king's court as part of his household (escuela, 'retinue'): the historical Diego and Fernán González figure as 'de schola regis' in charters of 1090 and 1105. deste çasamiento, so printed: the cedilla is clear on the scan, though the word is casamiento at vv. 1892 and 1937c; kept as Pidal prints it. avría, conditional of aver: 'I would have (no) wish for it'. The Çid's distrust is spoken at once.

sentences.t:
mas pues lo conseja el que más vale que nos,
fablemos en ello, en la poridad seamos nos.
Afé Dios del çielo que nos acuerde en lo mijor.”
sentences.l:
but since it counsels he who more is-worth than we,
let-us-speak in it, in the secret-counsel let-us-be we.
Behold God of-the heaven that us may-he-accord in the best.”
sentences.i: but since one who is worth more than we advises it, let us talk it over, and keep it among ourselves. May God in heaven guide us to what is best.”
sentences.n: el que más vale que nos, 'he who is worth more than we', the king; nos takes in the Çid's two counsellors. fablemos, subjunctive of exhortation, 'let us speak'. en la poridad seamos nos, 'let us be in secret council' (poridad, 'secrecy'). Afé, 'lo, behold' (= he aquí), here leading into a wish. Pidal's note: 'Dios nos aconseje lo mejor', 'may God counsel us the best'. acuerde, subjunctive of acordar, 'to bring to one mind, counsel'. mijor = mejor.

sentences.t:
—“Con todo esto, a vos dixo Alfons
que vos vernié a vistas do oviéssedes sabor;
querer vos ye ve[e]r e darvos su amor,
acordar vos yedes después a todo lo mejor.”
sentences.l:
—“With all this, to you said Alfons
that to-you he-would-come to meeting where you-might-have liking;
to-want you he-would to-see and to-give-you his love,
to-accord yourself you-would afterward to all the best.”
sentences.i: “Besides all this, Alfonso sends you word that he would come to meet you wherever you pleased; he would wish to see you and give you his favour, and afterwards you could agree on all that is best.”
sentences.n: Minaya speaks again. Con todo esto, 'with all this, besides'. vernié, conditional of venir (= vendría): venir + ie with n and r changing places (venrié > vernié), where modern Spanish puts in a d. Pidal's note: do oviéssedes sabor, 'donde gustéis', 'wherever you please' (oviéssedes, imperfect subjunctive of aver). querer vos ye, the split conditional: querríe + vos, 'he would want you'; ve[e]r = ver, the second e Pidal's (in italics). acordar vos yedes, split again: acordaríedes + vos, 'you would come to agreement'.

sentences.t:
Essora dixo el Çid: “plazme de coraçón.”
—“Estas vistas o las ayades vos,”
dixo Minaya, “vos se[e]d sabidor.”
sentences.l:
Then said the Çid: “it-pleases-me from heart.”
—“These meetings where them you-may-have you,”
said Minaya, “you be knower.”
sentences.i: Then the Çid said: “It pleases me with all my heart.” “Where this meeting is to be held,” said Minaya, “is yours to decide.”
sentences.n: plazme = plaze me, 'it pleases me' (plazer = placer). vistas, plural in form, one meeting in sense. Estas vistas … las, the object set first and taken up by las. o, 'where' (= do, donde); ayades, present subjunctive of aver, 'you may hold'. se[e]d, as at v. 1903. sabidor, 'knower': 'you are to know it', the choice the king left to the Çid at v. 1912.

sentences.t:
—“Non era maravilla si quisiesse el rey Alfons,
fasta do lo fallássemos buscar lo ir[i]emos nos,
por darle grand ondra commo a rey [e señor].
sentences.l:
—“Not it-was wonder if wished the king Alfons,
up-to where him we-might-find to-seek him we-would-go we,
for to-give-him great honour as to king [and lord].
sentences.i: “It would be no wonder if King Alfonso wished it: we would go and seek him wherever we might find him, to do him great honour as our king and lord.
sentences.n: The Çid answers. Pidal's note to v. 1951 gives the sense: if the king wished it and called him to his presence, he would go and seek him wherever he could find him (for the king had no fixed court or seat); but since the king honours him with a meeting, he fixes the place on the Tajo. Non era maravilla, 'it would be no wonder', imperfect for conditional. quisiesse, imperfect subjunctive of querer. fasta = hasta; fallássemos = hallásemos (f- for h-). buscar lo ir[i]emos, the split conditional: iríemos + lo, 'we would go to seek him', the i Pidal's (in italics). [e señor], Pidal's (in italics), the words of v. 1885.

sentences.t:
Mas lo que él quisiere, esso queramos nos.
Sobre Tajo, que es una agua [mayor],
ayamos vistas quando lo quiere mio señor.”
sentences.l:
But that which he may-wish, that let-us-want we.
Upon Tajo, which is a water [greater],
let-us-have meeting when it wants my lord.”
sentences.i: But whatever he wishes, let that be our wish. On the Tajo, which is a great river, let us hold our meeting, whenever my lord wills it.”
sentences.n: quisiere, future subjunctive of querer. queramos, present subjunctive, 'let us wish'; the final s is broken on the scan but there, and the sense needs it. Sobre Tajo, 'on the Tajo', the great river of central Spain, without the article. agua, 'water', here 'river'; [mayor], Pidal's (in italics). ayamos, present subjunctive of aver, 'let us have'. The Çid names the place; the king will name the day (Pidal's note to v. 1912).

sentences.t:
Escrivien cartas, bien las se[e]lló,
con dos cavalleros luego las enbió:
lo que el rey quisiere, esso ferá el Campeador.
sentences.l:
They-were-writing letters, well them he-sealed,
with two knights at-once them he-sent:
that which the king may-wish, that will-do the Campeador.
sentences.i: Letters were written; he sealed them well and sent them at once by two knights: whatever the king wishes, that the Campeador will do.
sentences.n: Escrivien, imperfect of escrivir in -ie (= escribían), plural, then se[e]lló and enbió, singular, the Çid: scribes write, the lord seals. se[e]lló = selló, the second e Pidal's (in italics). luego, 'at once' (not 'later'). ferá = hará, future of fer (f- for h-). The last verse gives what the letters say, and the tirada ends on the Çid's obedience; the king's answer opens tirada 103, in a new assonance (á-a).
